findings.text: the plan requires the shared rule to take the refused backend and skip it, but widest_fitting_candidate(candidates) takes only the list, so each caller re-implements the skip and reckon/crew/dispatch.py:710 returns the resolution unchanged when the refused lane is the widest usable - the exact return the plan says must be gone. It is excluded in the normal path by the context-fit reason the scan attaches to an oversized lane, so this is a latent hole rather than a live one, and the evidence fragment at line 25 claiming dispatch raises 'for every case instead of returning the resolution' overstates the code.

the refusal is still built from _competence_verdict when that verdict disallows, which the plan explicitly forbids ('Never build this refusal from routing._competence_verdict'); the payload is safe today because that verdict embeds the context-fit figures, but the branch is untested and is the shape the plan bans because such a verdict can be satisfied while the request is not.
